protocol.classificationSelection: Minimize worst selection FP/FN ratio to frozen v2 across overall, pooled irregular, and variable-routine windows, using one scalar threshold; tie-break average ratio then Brier score.
protocol.regressionSelection: Lowest selection +120-minute MAE across the same candidates; all four horizons use that candidate configuration.
protocol.calibration: Separate calibration identities: Platt probability map, global minimax FP/FN-ratio threshold, nominal90% residual bands. No routine label supplied to inference.
protocol.finalLock: Final2000..2119 and the held-out combination are not generated until all estimator/calibration/threshold/interval bytes are frozen and hashed.
protocol.primaryAggregate: The six familiar routine families; held-out parameter combination is reported separately.
limitations: All outcomes remain synthetic. Simultaneous FP/FN reductions are sought, not guaranteed on fresh patients.
The seven-regime aggregate includes six training families and one held-out parameter combination, not a new physiological simulator.
Unannounced future meals remain partly unpredictable from current observations.

limitations: All outcomes remain synthetic. Simultaneous FP/FN reductions are sought, not guaranteed on fresh patients.
The seven-regime aggregate includes six training families and one held-out parameter combination, not a new physiological simulator.
Unannounced future meals remain partly unpredictable from current observations.
No future meal annotations, latent simulator terms, routine labels or absolute clock values are predictors.
Synthetic HR includes contemporaneous meal response by simulator design; improved HR feature utility is not evidence of real-world meal detection.
FP and FN counts are overlapping exact-horizon windows, not deduplicated events or alarms per patient-day.
The alert threshold is an experimental error-tradeoff policy, not a clinically established action threshold.
The variable-routine and unseen-combination results must be read separately; pooled improvements do not establish uniform gains.
Confidence intervals resample identities and keep routine variants paired; they do not quantify simulator-to-clinic uncertainty.
Scenario controls remain illustrative arithmetic, not learned treatment effects.

reportingCorrections.detail: Removed MAE confidence intervals from observed-CGM/trajectory slices because the equal-window bootstrap helper does not match their unequal per-patient window counts. Point metrics, paired aggregate/case intervals, fitted model and policy are unchanged.
